units.text: Scale Pods when demand increases, and add node capacity when those Pods cannot be placed. The horizontal autoscaler changes the replica count; an eligible node autoscaler can respond to schedulable capacity shortages.
More Pods are not automatically more resilient. Check resource requests, topology, quotas and readiness. Spread healthy replicas so a single node failure does not take them all down.

When an application is unavailable, trace the failing layer before replacing infrastructure. Start with load balancer target health, then check ingress events, Pod readiness and logs, and finally node and control-plane evidence.

Metrics show trends, logs explain errors, events describe state changes, and traces follow requests. Correlate these signals for the same incident. Container Insights and control-plane logging need configuration before you rely on them.
App Runner illustrates a managed web deployment: it takes source or a supported container image and gives the application managed deployment, H T T P S, health checks and scaling.

New customers cannot adopt App Runner. Eligible existing customers can continue; for a new web service, evaluate E C S Express Mode. Neither choice eliminates the need to verify private dependencies and quotas.

Check eligibility before choosing the architecture. Existing App Runner customers can continue operating and creating eligible services. For new adoption, evaluate E C S Express Mode, which provides a streamlined E C S web deployment.

For a migration, deploy the same application image in the new environment, verify the domain and health checks, then shift traffic gradually with a rollback plan. A running container by itself does not prove the cutover is safe.

An App Runner V P C connector changes outbound application traffic. Use it for a private dependency such as R D S. If the application needs public endpoints, plan nat or appropriate service endpoints rather than assuming a public connector subnet solves it.
Choose inbound access independently. A public service URL remains public unless you separately configure the supported private ingress path. Verify both connections and authorization.

A multi-Region app needs three recovery plans. Replicate and verify image digests, deploy healthy compute independently, and choose the appropriate Dynamo D B global table consistency mode for the data requirements.

Test regional traffic shifts and failback with observable results. DNS caching can delay client movement. Do not assume every replica read is instantly current, and verify the behavior of the consistency mode you chose.

Use E C S Anywhere when the control plane should stay in AWS but containers must run on supported customer-owned hosts. Register the host with E C S and Systems Manager agents; you still own local compute and networking.

A brief disconnect can leave existing tasks running, but it interrupts reliable control. Check the regional link and external task limits, including supported network modes, before selecting this design.
For an external workload, register an eligible host and then let the regional E C S control plane schedule external tasks there. The host and its local infrastructure remain your responsibility.

If the regional connection drops, existing tasks may keep running. Restore connectivity before depending on new scheduling and management. Do not assume that A W S V P C or E C S service load balancing works for external tasks.

Choose E K S Anywhere when you need to operate Kubernetes control and worker nodes on your own infrastructure. The optional connection to AWS adds visibility without making AWS the operator of the local control plane.
For a supported disconnected environment, stage registry artifacts and dependencies before going offline. You still operate cluster upgrades, storage and workload health.

A disconnected E K S Anywhere cluster can operate locally on supported infrastructure. Prepare the required artifacts, mirror them into the local registry, and run the local control plane and workers.
Treat AWS console visibility as optional and separate. It does not host the Kubernetes control plane or remove your responsibility for disconnected lifecycle operations.

Cloud Map helps a client find where a service instance is currently registered. The backend registers its address and health information, and the client uses an eligible DNS or A P I lookup to get an endpoint.
The application connects to that backend directly. Check reachability and access independently; DNS caching and health configuration can affect how fresh the discovered endpoint is.
Follow the three actions: register the backend, discover its address, then connect directly to the backend. Cloud Map is not on the data path, so it does not replace network connectivity.
If discovery succeeds but the request fails, check endpoint freshness, routing and permissions. A DNS or A P I answer is not proof of authorization.

Use Service Connect for participating E C S workloads that need stable service names and managed proxies. The Cloud Map namespace supplies names and configuration; the proxies participate in the service traffic.
Clients and services still need supported connectivity and ports. Check security groups, and use available telemetry from the proxies to see whether requests reach their destination.
Distinguish configuration and traffic. Cloud Map provides the namespace and name; the participating E C S applications use managed proxies over a reachable network path to carry requests.
A stable name does not create a tunnel. Verify routes, ports and security groups, and provide a supported access path for nonparticipating clients.
AWS App Mesh is no longer a deployment choice. Preserve the requirements it illustrates: service traffic control, telemetry, identity and encryption, and handling failures safely.

Pick a current option based on those requirements: Service Connect for participating E C S services, V P C Lattice for suitable service networking, or a supported Kubernetes solution. Validate features rather than assuming these are interchangeable.

Use V P C Lattice when applications need managed service connectivity across eligible VPCs and accounts. A caller uses the service network to reach a registered healthy target, subject to connection and policy requirements.
When AWS I A M auth is enabled, verify policies and signed caller requests. An association only establishes the service connection option; it does not independently authorize the caller.
Troubleshoot Lattice in three gates: service association and network reachability, authorization when AWS I A M is enabled, and target health. A network path does not mean the caller is allowed.

If the request is rejected, check caller permissions and the signature at the authorization gate. If it reaches the service but targets are unhealthy, inspect their health checks. Use logs and metrics to separate these failures.
